transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you to see me?

Well... I guess I just keep forgetting things. Things I really shouldn’t. 

Like, uh... my heart follow-up appointments. Or remembering to call the clinic back. Even just... going to do a repair job and realizing I didn't bring the right tools with me. Just stuff like that.
Did these memory issues come on suddenly, or have they developed gradually over time?

Well... it's been causing real trouble for about a year and two months, I'd say. 

Ever since I had a cardiac scare. They made me cut back on my walking... and my projects. Just couldn't do as much. I guess staying busy with all that used to keep me settled. So... yeah. Since then.
Outside of those moments of forgetfulness, are you still able to manage everyday tasks like your finances and medications on your own?
Yeah... I suppose so. I mean, the bills get paid. And the pills... I just take them. It's mostly just... what I mentioned before. The rest is fine, I guess.
Over this past year, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless?
No... I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm not depressed or anything. Just... annoyed when I mess up, I guess. But no... I feel fine that way.
Have you been feeling anxious, nervous, or on edge?
No. Not really. I mean, I get a little restless, like I said, but... not anxious. Just... regular, I suppose.
Looking back to when you were a kid or in school, did you ever struggle with focus, forgetfulness, or restlessness?

Well... that was a long time ago. But... yeah, I suppose so. Even back in grade school, I guess I was the kid who couldn't stay in his seat. I'd, uh... blurt out answers. Got notes sent home to my folks for talking too much. So... yeah. Always been that way, I guess.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits chronic inattention and forgetfulness, along with a documented childhood history of motor hyperactivity, impulsivity (blurting out answers), and excessive talking dating back to grade school.
